claims.title: Binary-symplectic stabilizer-code distance characterization
claims.scope: finite n-qubit Pauli stabilizer codes generated by independent commuting Hermitian Paulis
assumptions: physical errors and observables are expanded in the n-qubit Pauli basis
nonclaims: binary normalizer dimension is not a parent-substrate storage cost
distance depends on the declared physical Pauli weight

claims.title: Code-distance local indistinguishability
claims.scope: all encoded density operators in one stabilizer code and every physical subset of fewer than d qubits
assumptions: d is the minimum Pauli weight in N(S) outside S
local observables are arbitrary operators supported on the selected physical subset
nonclaims: an adaptive protocol aggregating multiple local measurements may implement a higher-weight logical observable
does not imply the logical state is expensive to represent in an unknown parent substrate

claims.title: Quantum Singleton bound from two correctable erasures
claims.scope: finite quantum codes correcting every erasure of fewer than d physical qubits
assumptions: ordinary finite-dimensional quantum entropy identities and subadditivity apply
the encoded system has n qubits and logical dimension 2^k
nonclaims: the bound constrains internal quantum-code parameters rather than unknown parent physics
satisfying the numerical inequality alone does not prove that supplied generators define a valid code

claims.title: Encoded logical-label predictive geometry and memory
claims.scope: m independent stabilizer-code blocks restricted to a logical computational basis with declared logical-Z coordinate queries
assumptions: each selected logical-Z query returns its deterministic logical-basis eigenvalue
one finite renderer state determines one future logical-query law
nonclaims: the result is for discrete logical basis labels rather than arbitrary logical quantum states
logical predictive bits are not automatically parent RAM bits

claims.title: Five-qubit perfect-code exact bounded certificate
claims.scope: the four declared five-qubit stabilizer generators and bounded exact enumeration/state-vector checks
assumptions: the supplied Pauli generator strings use the repository qubit-order convention
normalizer enumeration and state-vector projection are run on exactly five qubits
nonclaims: a finite certificate is not a proof of a scalable code family
state-vector storage is an independent checker rather than the asserted optimal representation

claims.title: Three-qubit repetition code has full quantum distance one
claims.scope: the stabilizer span generated by ZZI and IZZ under arbitrary Pauli errors
assumptions: quantum distance counts every Pauli in the normalizer outside the stabilizer
ZII is an allowed physical Pauli
nonclaims: distance one does not deny protection against the selected bit-flip error set
classical repetition distance and full quantum distance are different notions
